scope.future: The future PCFL-13 template is dormant. It may be used only after a new predecessor-bound human authorization, exact-backend reruns, locked confirmation, all registered statistical/nonstatistical gates, fresh review, and a claim-specific human decision.
scope.external_validity: No template in this file supports external causal truth, external validity, general intelligence, developmental scaling, or an action-experience flywheel.

future_backend_rerun_gate.rule: A D0 scripted or synthetic PASS validates the reference checker only. It cannot be cited as evidence that a future backend is nonleaking, causally faithful, isolated, or constructively using memory.

baseline_reversal_policy.general_rule: Every comparator is evaluated on the same fixed confirmation pairs without complete-case deletion. A reversal cannot be hidden by the primary family, calibration selection, average-over-roster language, or a resource-equality claim.

comparators.reversal_or_gate_failure: Withdraw every positive action-improvement, useful-memory, retention, and complete-pipeline claim. Only a negative/no-confirmation disposition is legal.

comparators.reversal_or_margin_failure: FUTURE_PCFL13_BOUNDED_POSITIVE is forbidden; do not claim compiled experiential memory improves on direct-QA LoRA.
FUTURE_PCFL13_BOUNDED_POSITIVE is forbidden and the LoRA moat is absent. Report that the native linked baseline matched or won; do not claim general memory-system superiority.

comparators.reversal_beyond_margin: The parametric-transport claim fails. FUTURE_TEXT_ONLY_OR_NEGATIVE_TRANSPORT may be used if its own explicit-memory gates passed.

comparators.reversal: Do not claim the learned condition beats exact present-item inference or that lifetime memory was necessary. Any otherwise legal statement must disclose the reversal and remain limited to its named comparators.
Do not claim superiority to honest context, context-independent benefit, or a general retention advantage. A primary-gate result, if otherwise legal, must disclose CTX-C as the winning comparator.

comparators.role: hierarchical/context-summary baseline with recorded extra resources
comparators.reversal: Do not claim superiority to summarized context, best use of long histories, or general memory superiority. Disclose the winning baseline and unequal resources.

comparators.role: raw episodic retrieval through the common one-atom channel
comparators.reversal: Do not claim compiled memory beats raw retrieval or that compilation is necessary. The exact comparator reversal and resource vector must be reported.
Do not claim experiential compilation beats reflection/lesson memory or is the generally useful representation.
Do not claim protocol-level superiority to organized linked memory under the common channel.
Expected and descriptive only. Never describe proximity to L as memory evidence, and never use L to rescue a failed registered comparator.

baseline_reversal_policy.required_secondary_reversal_disclosure: If any of Bayes-N, CTX-C, CTX-H, R-rec, X-text, or A-common matches or exceeds E-LoRA, append exactly: 'The following registered comparator arms matched or exceeded E-LoRA on the locked deck: {comma-separated arm IDs in baseline-manifest order}. No superiority to those comparators or general best-memory claim is made.'
baseline_reversal_policy.resource_rule: Equal source bytes or equal model-visible reader returns never license fixed-memory, fixed-compute, capacity-equivalence, or efficiency language. Every reversal and non-reversal remains resource-ledger-qualified.

normalization: Normalize strings to Unicode NFC before comparison.
For adversarial-corpus lookup only, casefold, map every Unicode dash to ASCII hyphen, collapse ASCII whitespace runs to one space, and trim.
Do not rewrite report bytes or use normalization to accept a non-exact allowed template.
acceptance: A report claim field must name one exact_allowed_templates claim_id and its claim text must byte-equal that template after NFC, including punctuation.
Every listed condition for that claim_id must have a hash-bound machine receipt with PASS disposition.
If a secondary baseline reversal occurred, the exact required disclosure is appended with comparator IDs in frozen baseline-manifest order.
No free-form headline, abstract, summary, caption, conclusion, tag, or metadata claim is permitted outside an exact template.
linter_algorithm.negative_disclaimer_exception: Forbidden terms may occur only inside the immutable negating/disclaimer sentence of an exact allowed template. Free-form negation is not an exception because a headline can launder a forbidden claim while appearing to deny it.
rejection: Reject a missing fixed-deck, post-working-window, operational-support, comparator, or resource qualifier where required.
Reject a D0 statement that attributes leakage absence, composition, discovery, transport, retention, binding, or action improvement to a future model/backend.
Reject an otherwise exact positive template if a baseline-reversal or negative-decision receipt forbids it.
Reject any untemplated scientific prose for mandatory fresh human semantic review; lexical nonmatch is not interpreted as safe.
linter_algorithm.semantic_limit: A string scanner cannot prove semantic safety. Exact-template-only claim fields plus fresh human review are mandatory; the paraphrase corpus is an adversarial regression suite, not an exhaustive language model.
